gauntlet: question
I need to correct a premise from the gathered draft before we go further. The draft says the existing settings resolver cannot accept overrides. Primary code shows otherwise: `settings/resolver.ts:11` already accepts a timeout override. I also traced every caller, and each one reads settings through that same resolver. So the missing timeout override is not a resolver limitation. The caller that needs the timeout is simply not passing its override to the resolver. The design will go forward on this corrected fact unless you override it in your reply. I'm recording it in the draft for `## Problem`.

This changes how the ask should be framed. A second settings file would add a parallel settings boundary beside the resolver that already owns all settings and is already used by every caller. It would also only paper over the real gap. No ticket decision settles this point. Which direction should the design take?

A) as framed: add a second settings file that carries the timeout override.
B) pivot: change the existing caller to pass its timeout override through `settings/resolver.ts:11`. This fixes the root cause on the resolver that already supports the override, with one settings path and no new boundary.
C) smaller or none: ship no settings change and document how to pass the timeout override through the existing resolver. If nothing ships, the timeout override stays missing for that caller.

Recommendation: B - the resolver already accepts the override and every caller uses it, so fixing the caller removes the gap without duplicating the settings boundary.
